Question: What are the advantages of being selfish?
Answer: I cried my lungs out when my roompartner called me fake. He knew me for three years. And this was what I got in return for all the good things I did for him. BUT He was right. I'm still fake. I sometimes fake my kindness. I sometimes fake the good replies on Quora. I sometimes reply in the best possible way even when I don't feel like. I listen to people's problems. And even though my mind is about to burst, I'm patient like a wall. I've read many books on death and it helped me. No one wants to die being a jerk. When people know they are about to die, they BECOME kind. They want to be remembered as a good man. And so do I. When I die, I want to be remembered as 'Oh, that guy? He was the kindest soul I knew.’ We don't wake up one day and become kind. We need to practice it every single day. Even when we're feeling shitty. Even when our mind is about to explode. You shouldn't explode on others just because your manager is toxic. You smile. You help people. You become kind. Aren't we all dying? Aren't our days getting less? Don't you want to be remembered as a good guy? That's selfish, yes. But being kind doesn't harm anyone. Faking kindness doesn't harm anyone. It all starts will faking. And slowly, it starts running in your veins. You become humble. You become patient. You become the best version of yourself. (This book was written by a dying man. He had cancer. But the irony is everyone is dying. Everyone is inching towards death.) We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: Is life easy or hard?
Answer: 'He cheated on me,' she said. 'For a better-looking girl.’ 'Who was the girl?’ I asked. 'My best friend.’ 'I'm so sorry.’ 'That's okay.’ 'And what do you think, is she better looking than you?’ 'I don't know. But after he left me, I start hating my body. I started doubting myself that I'm not enough. I started to think that I was ugly.’ 'See, I don't know how you look. But despite that, I can say that you're beautiful. In a race between pretty and beautiful, beautiful will always win, eventually, don't you think?’ 'I hope so.’ 'Also, if we can't think good about ourselves, then surviving becomes a really tough act.’ 'Agree. But, looks do matter, right?’ she asked. 'I'd be a sweet liar if I say it doesn't. Looks matter. Yes. If you're a girl, it matters a lot. I've seen a couple of good-looking girls who talk stupid yet they get a lot of male attention. While, on the other hand, girls with the kindest souls get ignored just because they don't look stunning and their features are not hot and curvy.’ 'And?’ 'And I think it's the toughest of all. If you're a guy, you can earn good money to compensate for your facial features. You can get arranged easily. But if you're a girl who dreams of getting married, someday, but your prettiness doesn't align with society, then you'll have a really tough time. You'll find it hard for a guy to like you. And you'll find it hard to even qualify for an arranged marriage.’ 'Then what do we do?’ she asked. 'Accept. Work on the things that you can change. Grow yourself as a person. And let go of the things that are not in your control. Looks, I think, can't be changed. It can be enhanced a bit by exercising. But it can't be totally altered. So if something is not in our control, can't we just stop fretting about it?’ 'We can and we must. I totally agree. Also, you know that you're doing a really good job, right?’ she said. 'I know,' I replied. ‘Thank you so much.’ We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: What are your experiences traveling alone?
Answer: When I first thought of travelling solo, I thought people would judge me. I thought they would see me as a heartbroken guy or a loner. Except, it wasn't true. It was all in my head. Everyone's eyes glitter up when they hear I travel solo. People look at me with admiration. They say I want to travel solo, as well, but I'm afraid of being bored. They say whenever I think of travelling solo someone accompanies me. I reply that the same happens with me but you need to say no. I planned this trip to Udaipur, solo, and when I told my plans to a girl, she asked if I was okay with her travelling with me. I refused politely. She's really sweet. A girl who gives you space and splits the bill. But I said I really like to travel alone. She understood it. Same happened with another girl. She said if you would've told me earlier I could have come along. Except, I don't want anyone to come along. I make friends in solo-travel. I go solo and when I return back, I have 40+ contacts on my mobile. That's crazy. I consider myself an introvert and that's really crazy. Solo-travel is all about living on your own terms. I slept enough so that I could function properly. I sat in the ghats on Udaipur, today, for three hours or so. And now I'm sitting on the rooftop, alone, with a view like this. Travel solo. It's addictive. And once you love your own company, you don't get hurt overly. Again and again. I've experienced this. And I don't want anyone to go through it no matter how me-centric this post sounds. We all are gifted, Shubham KP

Question: How are your Diwali preparations going?
Answer: 22nd January is claimed to be the biggest Dipawali in India so far. And I can sense it. A group of people came to our flat a month ago and gave us rice and a pamphlet for free. They asked us to place a diya in our home. I went outside today and met a guy. He said he'll apply for sick leave tomorrow. He was holding two flags of Jai Shree Ram and was glittering with joy. There are rallies. There are Bhandaraas. There is literally a Diwali-like vibe in our locality. And even though I'm an atheist, I like the feeling that everyone around me is beaming with joy. I'm not that atheist who doesn't respect people's sentiments. Instead, I feel elated when everyone around me is celebrating no matter what the reason is. One of my friends had put a status on WhatsApp of the Ram Mandir anthem sung by Kailash Kher. I watched it and I cried. People struggled a lot for this day. I'm not going into the historical or political debate over this. Because it's a never-ending discussion. I just want to say that if you're someone who gets happiness from other's happiness, tomorrow is one of your days. (My friend's small mandir) We all are gifted, Shubham KP
